controls.label: Gain
controls.tip: Preamp gain, 0 to +60 dB. The hardware prints 20 to 60 dB on this knob (0 to 40 with the pad in); the plugin starts at 0 because a DAW track is not a microphone. Raise it to push the tube harder. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Tube
controls.tip: Tube rolling: ten cat tubes on three real tube types (12AU7, 12AT7, 12AX7, new and aged), each with its type shown. The tube stage is a Koren triode model with the published parameters of its type; the differences between the 12AX7 cats and the ageing are our voicing on top, scaled by Variation. The tube in the ART unit is not stated in its manual, so the default is a typical choice, unverified.

controls.label: Pad -20
controls.tip: Lowers the preamp gain by 20 dB for hot signals.

controls.label: Invert
controls.tip: Flips the phase 180 degrees at the preamp output.

controls.label: Low cut
controls.tip: 100 Hz high-pass filter, 6 dB per octave: removes rumble, pops and wind noise and still sounds natural.

controls.label: Impedance
controls.tip: On the hardware this loads your microphone (150 Ohm to 3.4 kOhm). In the plugin there is no mic, so this is a tone control of our own modelling, not mic loading: about -3 dB (150 Ohm) to +3 dB (3.4 kOhm) smooth tilt of the top, with a gentle opposite body change around 220 Hz. The dotted line in the EQ view shows it; the readout shows the top change. The real physical effect (source resistance with the tube input capacitance, which we computed) is far above the audible range, so it is not what you hear here. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Tube voltage
controls.tip: NORMAL adds warmth with more tube saturation at higher levels. HIGH gives more gain, headroom and bandwidth. The change is gradual, 10 to 20 seconds, like the hardware.

controls.label: Voicing
controls.tip: Plugin extra, not on the hardware. Strength of the selected tube's own voicing: tone, bandwidth, supply sag and gain trim. 100 % = the tube's base voicing, 0 % = neutral, 200 % = double, 300 % = extreme (very dark or bright, heavy sag). Works for every tube. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Colour
controls.tip: Plugin extra, not on the hardware. Tube colour, from angelic to nasty, at any level (you hear it even at low Gain). 0 = clean tube only. Up to about 50 % it adds warm even harmonics; above that it adds more and more grit, and 100 % is heavy, fuzzy and aggressive. Voicing and Gain still shape the tube itself. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Variation
controls.tip: Plugin extra, not on the hardware. How different the tubes sound from each other. This is an exaggeration factor on the voicing differences (tone, gain, bandwidth, supply sag, noise), 0 % = the tubes sound almost alike, 30 % = a clear difference, 100 % = five times the voicing difference (extreme). It is not a measured value. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Vintagenoise
controls.tip: Adds the tube's own noise floor, quiet or noisy depending on the tube (from retailer noise ratings, mapped by us to a level, so a rough guide only). Off by default.

controls.label: Threshold
controls.tip: Level above which the compressor works. The unit prints -40 to +20 dB here; we read that as dBu and show dBFS (0 VU = +4 dBu = -20 dBFS), so -64 to -4 dBFS. Also draggable on the Dynamics view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Ratio
controls.tip: How much the signal above the threshold is reduced. Fully left is off (1:1). A good start for vocals is 2.5:1. 20:1 makes it a limiter. Also draggable on the Dynamics view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: De-ess amt
controls.tip: How hard the esses are pushed down: the value is the deepest reduction, OFF to -20 dB as printed on the unit. The threshold is automatic and follows the programme (it tracks the average level of the detected band), so more Amount is simply more de-essing; no threshold to set. Split band: only the band around De-ess Hz is reduced. The hardware prints OFF, -6, -14, -20 dB on this knob. The threshold. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Expander /gate.
controls.tip: Expand: a gentle downward expander at the hardware slope, 1:1.5. Gate: fast open, auto hold, release, with an on/off decision and a built-in 4 dB hysteresis, down to the Range floor. The threshold knob below switches it on; fully left (OFF) it is out of the path.

controls.label: Attack
controls.tip: How fast the compressor reacts. The hardware goes from 0.25 ms (dot) to 100 ms; the plugin goes down to 0.05 ms as an extra. Short can sound thin or pumping; longer lets the punch of a snare through. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Release
controls.tip: How fast the gain comes back. Log scale, so the fast region 0.1 to 100 ms has most of the travel. The hardware range is 100 ms to 3 s (the 3 s end is the unit's real limit): the dot marks 100 ms, and the Hardware range switch restores 100 ms to 3 s. Below 100 ms is a plugin extra; very fast release adds only the distortion any fast release causes (tested). Double-click resets.

controls.label: De-ess Hz
controls.tip: Centre of the detector band-pass and of the band that is reduced, 2 kHz to 15 kHz (as printed on the unit). About 6 kHz suits most voices. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Exp./gate thresh.
controls.tip: The expander or gate works below this level (dBFS, after the input trim). Fully left is OFF: the expander or gate is out of the signal path, as on the unit. The hardware prints OFF, -22 to +20 dB; read as dBu that is -46 to -4 dBFS. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Auto
controls.tip: Program dependent release (plugin extra): fast for short peaks, slow for sustained sound. The Release knob sets the base time.

controls.label: HW range
controls.tip: Plugin extra. Restores the hardware release range, 100 ms to 3 s. Off = the plugin range 0.1 ms to 1 s.

controls.label: Input trim
controls.tip: Plugin extra, not on the hardware (the manual has no input control for the dynamics). Level into the expander, gate and compressor, so you can drive the compressor harder or softer without touching the tube. Minus 18 to plus 18 dB. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Makeup
controls.tip: Plugin extra, not on the hardware (the manual has no compressor output control). Gain after the compressor. With Auto makeup on, the plugin adds the static gain that the current threshold, ratio and knee remove at 6 dB over the threshold, on top of this knob. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Automakeup
controls.tip: Adds makeup gain automatically from the threshold and ratio (plugin extra).

controls.label: Mix
controls.tip: Parallel compression: blends the compressed signal with the uncompressed one. 100 % = fully compressed. Double-click resets.

controls.label: TPlimiter
controls.tip: A lookahead true-peak safety limiter at the very end, ceiling -1 dBFS, 1.5 ms lookahead. On by default. Adds about 1.5 ms latency, which the plugin reports to the DAW.

controls.label: Range
controls.tip: Plugin extra. The most the gain is reduced: how deep the gate closes (the floor), 0 to -80 dB. Also limits the expander. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Release
controls.tip: Plugin extra. How fast the gain closes, 0.1 ms to 2 s. Very fast is a hard chop (an effect). Double-click resets.

controls.label: EQ position
controls.tip: Puts the EQ before (pre comp) or after (post comp) the expander and compressor. Pre helps when the signal has too much low or high content for the compressor; Post shapes the finished sound.

controls.label: EQ bypass
controls.tip: Sets the EQ flat without losing its settings.

controls.label: Mid-1 Hz
controls.tip: Bell, tunable from 100 Hz to 3 kHz. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Mid-2 Hz
controls.tip: Bell, tunable from 500 Hz to 15 kHz. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Low frequency
controls.tip: Low shelf, 50 or 150 Hz turnover.

controls.label: High frequency
controls.tip: High shelf, 5 or 15 kHz turnover.

controls.label: Low
controls.tip: Low shelf gain. Plus or minus 15 dB. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Mid-1
controls.tip: Mid-1 bell gain. Plus or minus 15 dB. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Mid-2
controls.tip: Mid-2 bell gain. Plus or minus 15 dB. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: High
controls.tip: High shelf gain. Plus or minus 15 dB. Also draggable on the EQ view. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Low slope
controls.tip: Low shelf slope (shelf Q). Higher = steeper with a small overshoot. Plugin extra; the manual does not give the hardware value, 0.7 is our assumption (a smooth shelf). Double-click resets.

controls.label: Mid-1 Q
controls.tip: Mid-1 bell width. Low Q = wide and gentle, high Q = narrow. 0.9 is our assumption for the unit (a broad musical bell; the manual does not state it). Scroll on the dot in the EQ view to change it. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Mid-2 Q
controls.tip: Mid-2 bell width. 0.9 is our assumption (the manual does not state it). Scroll on the dot in the EQ view to change it. Double-click resets.

controls.label: High slope
controls.tip: High shelf slope (shelf Q). Plugin extra; 0.7 is our assumption. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Output level
controls.tip: Gain or attenuation after the processing, to match your system level. As on the unit: fully left is off (-inf), the centre is 0 dB, fully right is +20 dB. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Power
controls.tip: Lit = the channel is processing. Click to bypass the whole channel (the same as Before in the preview rig).
Previous preset.

controls.label: Init
controls.tip: Open the preset list: factory presets and your own. Factory presets are starting points, set them by ear.
Next preset.

controls.label: Save
controls.tip: Save the current settings (and your recall notes) as your own preset. Stays on this device.
Delete, export or import your presets.

controls.label: Guide
controls.tip: Quick guide: what each view and control does.

controls.label: Settings
controls.tip: Info bubbles, eco mode and the look (colour theme).

controls.label: About & Support
controls.tip: About Studio 87, privacy, and ways to support the project.

controls.label: EQ
controls.tip: EQ curve with the live spectrum. Drag a dot: up and down is the gain, left and right is the frequency (the low and high bands snap between their two choices). Shortcut: 1.

controls.label: Dynamics
controls.tip: Compressor and expander curve: input on the bottom, output up the side. Drag the corner for the threshold, the end for the ratio, the lower dot for the expander or gate threshold. Shortcut: 2.

controls.label: Tube
controls.tip: The tube: its transfer curve, the harmonics it adds at the current level, and its bandwidth. Reacts to the tube type, Colour, voltage and gain. Shortcut: 3.

controls.label: GR history
controls.tip: Gain reduction history of the compressor and the expander or gate. Shortcut: 4.

controls.label: Signal flow
controls.tip: Signal flow of the unit. Click the EQ block to move the EQ before or after the dynamics. Shortcut: 5.

controls.label: Recall notes
controls.tip: Recall notes: write down your hardware settings, the microphone and the room. Saved with the plugin and with presets. Shortcut: 6.

controls.label: Test signal
controls.tip: Pick what the preview rig plays into the channel. 'Voice in a noisy room' has real pauses and a steady background noise, so the expander or gate has something to do. 'S sounds' is for the de-esser. 'Your file' uses the file you loaded.
options: Voice in a noisy room (gaps + background noise)

controls.label: Play
controls.tip: Start or stop the test signal. Shortcut: Space.

controls.label: Load file
controls.tip: Load your own audio file (wav, mp3, flac, ogg). It stays in this browser tab and is never uploaded.

controls.label: Input trim
controls.tip: Level into the plugin, like the track gain in your DAW. This is the preview rig, not a plugin control. Double-click resets.

controls.label: Before / After
controls.tip: Flip between the unprocessed input (Before) and the processed signal (After). Shortcut: B. With Match level on, both play at the same loudness, so you judge the sound and not the volume. A short crossfade avoids clicks.

controls.label: Match level
controls.tip: Applies an automatic gain offset to the Before signal so it has the same perceived loudness as After. Uses K-weighted (ITU BS.1770) short-term loudness, smoothed over about a second, so it does not pump. Preview rig feature.

controls.label: Hear the difference
controls.tip: Plays only what the processing adds or removes (After minus Before, with the Before level matched when Match level is on). A quick way to hear what the channel does. Preview rig feature.

controls.label: VU meter
controls.tip: Analog style VU meter. 0 VU is -20 dBFS here, like the hardware (0 VU is +4 dBu there).

controls.label: Tube name and description
controls.tip: High gain 12AX7 type (mu about 100). Our voicing: balanced, tight, a little less bass weight, silky top, low noise. Built on the published triode physics of its type; the flavour differences between the 12AX7 cats are our voicing.

controls.label: Gain reduction meter
controls.tip: Compressor gain reduction in dB, like the LED bar on the unit. The round light at the right is the expander or gate: dim for the first 5 dB of reduction, bright above that or when the gate is closed.

controls.label: Input and output level meters
controls.tip: Input and output level in dBFS: coloured bar is the level, white line is the peak, held for 2 seconds.

controls.label: Voltage change
controls.tip: The tube voltage moves gradually after you switch it, 10 to 20 seconds, so you hear the change settle.

controls.label: Window size read-out
controls.tip: Window size. Drag any edge or corner of the plugin to resize it; the shape stays the same. Double-click here for 100 %.

controls.label: Loudness readout
controls.tip: Integrated loudness in LUFS (ITU BS.1770, gated) of the unprocessed input and the processed output since you pressed Play, and the matched offset in dB. Click to reset the measurement.

controls.label: Preview rig label
controls.tip: Preview only: the plugin processes your DAW's audio. Mono unit: stereo tracks get the same processing on both sides.

dialogs.Guide:
QUICK GUIDE
SIGNAL PATH

Input, preamp (gain, tube, low cut, invert), then the EQ (if set to pre), the expander or gate, the compressor with de-esser, the EQ (if set to post) and the output level.

VIEWS
EQ: drag the four dots. Double-click a dot to flatten it.
Dynamics: drag the threshold, the ratio end and the expander or gate dot.
Tube: see what the tube does at your level: curve, harmonics, bandwidth.
GR history, Signal flow, Recall notes.
TUBES
Ten cat tubes on three tube types, from Clean to Heavy; Variation sets how different they are. The Colour knob scales the effect from almost clean to the full voicing.
Tube voltage Normal adds warmth; High gives more gain and headroom. The change settles over 10 to 20 seconds.
START HERE
Press Play, pick a preset, raise Gain to push the tube, and judge by ear.
Use Compare: bypass to hear what changed.
CLOSE
dialogs.About & Support:
ABOUT & SUPPORT

Purrr Voice Channel by Studio 87, AGPL-3.0-or-later. This page is a design mockup that plays test signals in your browser.

A tube channel strip for voices and instruments: a tube preamp with ten selectable tubes, an expander or gate, a compressor and limiter with de-esser, and a four band EQ that can sit before or after the dynamics. Made as a software companion to a hardware channel strip. All voicing is our own; nothing is measured from any real tube or unit.

SUPPORT

If it helps your music, a coffee on Ko-fi keeps new plugins coming.

☕ SUPPORT STUDIO 87 ON KO-FI
